subtitleNullable: Citizen Grievance Classification Dataset mapped to CPGRAMS-style categories
descriptionNullable:
## Overview
A synthetic dataset of citizen grievances written in Hindi, Hinglish
(Romanized Hindi), and English — the way complaints are actually typed on
government portals in India. Each grievance is labeled with a department
category aligned to CPGRAMS (Centralized Public Grievance Redress and
Monitoring System) conventions.

Built to train text classification models that automatically route citizen
grievances to the correct department and can assist in drafting formal
complaint text from informal citizen input — directly supporting regional-
language citizen service use cases (grievance redressal, education,
agriculture advisories) named in MeitY's Bhashini/VoicERA initiative.

## Files
- `grievances_synthetic.csv` — main dataset (~3,000 rows) for training/testing.
- `grievances_holdout_templates.csv` — a harder evaluation set built from
  sentence structures never seen in the main file, for honestly measuring
  model generalization rather than template memorization.

## Columns
- `grievance_id` — unique identifier
- `text` — the grievance text (mixed Hindi/Hinglish/English)
- `category` — one of 14 department categories (Water Supply, Electricity,
  Roads & Infrastructure, Sanitation & Garbage, Pension & Provident Fund,
  Land Records & Revenue, Police & Law and Order, Healthcare & Hospitals,
  Education & Schools, Ration & PDS, Banking & Financial Services,
  Corruption & Bribery, Employment & Labour, Municipal Certificates)

## Notes on synthetic generation
Text is template-generated with randomized locations, names, timeframes,
and amounts drawn from Indian-context reference pools, plus light informal
noise (spelling variants, mixed prefixes/suffixes) to approximate real
citizen writing style. Intended as a starting point for model development;
production use should be validated against real (anonymized) grievance data.

## Intended use
Multi-class text classification / grievance routing systems, particularly
for regional-language NLP research and citizen-service automation.
